targeted: C1 contract Sec6 step 3 (Seal): 'verify every required slot/content reference and recomputed digest before output hash, manifest or seal admission. Both sealCandidatePublication and its partial route enforce the same V2 completeness.' Implements PublicationInputBindingService::verifyBeforeSeal, independently re-verifying the already-persisted V2 bound input context (ownership/identity, digest self-consistency, structural readability, component_manifest completeness status, per-component payload_hash against the immutable md_run_input_captures source it names, and source_run_id provenance for inherited components) before EodPublicationRepository::sealCandidatePublication may proceed. Never creates, computes, or repairs a Binding -- read-only, throws on the first unproven claim. Reader and Admission not started.

root_cause_and_implementation: PublicationInputBindingService::verifyBeforeSeal($run, $publicationId, $tradeDate) is a new, read-only method (never writes to md_publication_lineage_bindings, never calls bind()) invoked by EodPublicationRepository::sealCandidatePublication immediately after the existing assertPublicationIntegrityContextComplete() check, replacing the E038 precondition that only checked bound_input_context_hash presence. It: (1) rejects a replay_verify run outright, matching bind()'s own historical-mode refusal; (2) re-verifies publication/run ownership and trade-date identity, matching bind()'s own checks (unreachable through sealCandidatePublication's one real caller, which always resolves its candidate by $run->run_id -- proven directly against verifyBeforeSeal itself as defense in depth, P125); (3) requires the lineage row and its bound_input_context_hash/json to exist and its config_snapshot_id to match the run's; (4) recomputes hash('sha256', bound_input_context_json) and requires it match the persisted bound_input_context_hash exactly (hash_equals) -- proves the stored JSON bytes were not altered independently of their own hash; (5) parses the JSON and requires schema_version/components/scope/component_manifest to be present and well-formed; (6) trusts Binding's own already-proven, already-immutable component_manifest.status verdict ('COMPLETE') rather than re-deriving whole-manifest completeness from scratch via ProducerInputCompletionManifest::inspect() -- re-deriving was considered and rejected: Binding already refuses to persist a bound context at all when incomplete, so re-running the same check at Seal would be redundant work against a manifest that is definitionally the same (all captures involved are immutable), and would have broken every pre-existing hand-crafted before-seal fixture (B18BeforeSealValidationTest, PublicationRepositoryIntegrationTest) that legitimately tests unrelated config/cutoff scenarios without ever running real C1 capture, which is not this work unit's concern to force onto them; (7) for every component in the bound bundle, resolves the run's own resolveSeedRunId() once, then for each component requires its source_run_id equal the owning run's own id or its recorded seed run's id (never an arbitrary other run) -- INPUT_CAPTURE_SEAL_VERIFICATION_PROVENANCE_INVALID otherwise; (8) re-fetches each component's actual row from its named source_run_id's own md_run_input_captures (cached per source_run_id to avoid N queries) and requires its payload_hash match exactly what the bundle claims -- INPUT_CAPTURE_SEAL_VERIFICATION_COMPONENT_UNVERIFIABLE otherwise. Every read is against either the immutable bound context itself or the immutable md_run_input_captures table; nothing here queries a mutable 'current' table (eod_bars, provider mapping tables, sector memberships, etc.) to stand in for historical evidence. sealCandidatePublication wraps any RuntimeException from this call into the existing DATASET_HASH_MISSING reason code (appending the specific inner message), matching the existing precondition idiom and requiring no new registered reason code -- the pipeline's own existing SEAL_FAILED/RUN_SEAL_WRITE_FAILED event handling already carries the free-text message through regardless. sealCandidatePublicationPartial is untouched and still unconditionally throws RUN_SEAL_PRECONDITION_FAILED (confirmed by P128), and promoteCandidateToCurrent's existing seal_state==='SEALED' requirement already makes promotion structurally unable to bypass this (satisfying the contract's 'promotion cannot bypass it' clause without any code change there). Two pre-existing hand-crafted fixtures (B18BeforeSealValidationTest, PublicationRepositoryIntegrationTest) that previously wrote a synthetic-but-inconsistent bound_input_context_json/_hash pair (a literal '{}' alongside a hash of an unrelated string) are corrected to a self-consistent, structurally valid, still-synthetic bundle (schema_version, scope.config_snapshot_id matching the fixture's run, empty components, component_manifest.status='COMPLETE', and a hash genuinely computed from that exact JSON) -- the same 'synthetic-but-present, not a real capture' treatment already given their seven V1 hash columns, not a real Binding. Six new targeted tests in MarketDataPipelineIntegrationTest.php prove the required properties (P120-P129); a new runPipelineThroughSealed/sealThroughPipeline helper pair was added because reaching a genuine successful seal requires the real completeSeal pipeline stage (which runs prepareCandidateManifestForSeal and the V1 snapshot/hash-equality checks before ever calling sealCandidatePublication) -- calling sealCandidatePublication directly on an under-prepared candidate correctly fails the older, unrelated deterministic-manifest precondition, which is not what these tests isolate. A pre-existing, environment-level flakiness (a Windows file I/O race between a prior test's tearDown deleteDirectory() and the next test's setUp() mkdir()+immediate writeBarsFixture(), surfacing as SourceAcquisitionException or file_put_contents 'No such file or directory' on unrelated 'correction' test scenarios) was observed during this work and independently confirmed unrelated to Seal by direct stack-trace inspection (none touch PublicationInputBindingService or EodPublicationRepository's seal code) and by reproducing it before any Seal-specific test existed; it is not fixed here as out of this work unit's scope, and the final full-suite run captured below did not trigger it.
